sources.entry: TiddlyWiki - Reusable non-linear personal web notebook. (Source Code) BSD-3-Clause Nodejs

summary.one_liner: TiddlyWiki is a non-linear personal web notebook: a complete interactive wiki written in JavaScript that runs as a single HTML file in the browser or as a Node.js application.
summary.what_it_does: TiddlyWiki stores content as small named units called tiddlers and lets you link and edit them in a non-linear way. It can be used as a single self-contained HTML file in a browser, or run under Node.js as a server or client/server setup. The README describes a command-line interface that processes arguments left to right, with commands such as --listen to serve a wiki, --build to produce an offline HTML copy, and --render to save tiddlers as static HTML. Plugins can be loaded from the command line with + or ++ prefixes. The user interface is itself implemented in WikiText, which the README describes as hackable. Upgrades are handled through npm, and specific older versions can be installed by version number.
use_cases: generating static HTML sites from wiki content
offline single-file wiki in a browser
serving a wiki over a local network with Node.js
how_to_run: Install Node.js (for example: apt install nodejs on Debian/Ubuntu, or brew install node on Mac)
notable: Whole wiki fits in a single HTML file that works in a browser
Entire user interface is written in hackable WikiText
Command-line commands run in sequence and support plugin loading with + and ++ prefixes
Can generate static HTML sites from tiddlers via --render
Official developer documentation and community forums are linked from the README
caveats: Advanced client/server configuration is aimed at advanced users and developers
Debian-based systems may need a symlink from nodejs to node to run the tool
Developer documentation is described as still in progress
keywords: make a wiki i can host myself
